perspective:
Christian Mensah’s accessible information:

- He is a police officer; Jonathan is his childhood best friend. Their bond is strong, and Christian often seeks Jonathan’s advice and values his perspective.
- Christian had been feeling that Jonathan was hiding something important. This made him anxious and suspicious, so he arranged a meeting at their favorite coffee shop to confront Jonathan.
- At the meeting, Christian told Jonathan he felt something serious was being hidden. Jonathan said Christian could trust him, but then admitted he had been keeping something: he was in trouble and did not know how to tell Christian.
- Christian felt worried and empathetic, offered help, and said they could face it together. Jonathan thanked him, said the situation was complicated and he did not want to drag Christian in, but then said he could use support/resources and needed to get out of the mess.
- Christian came to believe the trouble might involve criminal activity. He asked Jonathan if it was illegal. Jonathan said he could not say for sure, might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but said he himself did not do anything illegal. Christian said he would look into it discreetly.
- Through his own investigation, Christian concluded that Jonathan was being framed by someone trying to set him up. He told Jonathan this, said he was not sure yet who was responsible but had leads, and planned to gather evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence.
- Christian later believed/found out that the real culprit was someone close to both him and Jonathan. He told Jonathan he had found out who was behind it—someone they both knew and trusted—and said he would confront them and bring them to justice. Jonathan warned him the person was dangerous but trusted Christian to do what was right.
- The specific identity of the culprit is not named in the dialogue Christian has with Jonathan. Christian’s knowledge of the culprit comes from his own investigation, not from Jonathan’s direct disclosure in these scenes.
